title: Answer a question using evidence
objective: Clarify a question, answer with evidence, and state what you cannot tell.

slides.title: Take the question in three steps
body: Listen to the whole question. If part is unclear, ask the listener to repeat it.
Answer the part your evidence supports. Say what extra information would help with the rest.

slides.title: Listen to an honest answer
body: Audience: “Were more frogs seen after dark? Why?”
Presenter: “Yes. We saw 6 after dark and 2 before dark in our time periods.”
“We did not measure the reason. We could repeat the counts and record the conditions.”

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Your team counted 12 snails near a pond and 5 near a stream on one day. An audience member asks, “Where did you see more snails? Is it always like that?”

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Ask the speaker to repeat or clarify part of the question.
Answer the first question directly. Include both counts.
Try: Could you repeat the part about ___?

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Your team counted 11 bees in a park and 4 in a field on one day. An audience member asks, “Where did you see more bees? Is it always like that?”

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Ask the speaker to repeat or clarify part of the question.
Answer the first question directly. Include both counts.
Answer the second question. Give one limit and one next step.

slides.title: Try a harder follow-up
body: Ask your partner one question the data cannot answer. Listen for an honest limit and one useful next step.
